newsitem.title: USA: Brazil 97/8 orange juice output 1.25 MMT --attache.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97/8 orange juice output 1.25 MMT --attache.

text.p: An agricultural attache at the American embassy in Sao Paulo pegged Brazil 1997/98 orange juice output at 1.25 million tonnes, up 9.6 percent from the previous season and slightly above the official U.S. Agriculture Department forecast.

In a report dated June 5 that was released in Washington on Monday, the attache said the forecast for oranges processing in 1997/98 was 303 million boxes, with Sao Paulo accounting for 295 million boxes.
The attache said Sao Paulo processing plants should contribute 1.22 million tonnes of FCOJ due to the greater volume of oranges for processing.
The 1997/98 processing season is likely to be short, ending by mid-December, due to the concentrated and uniform flowering in Septmber and October 1996, the attache wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data. In a report on June 2, USDA forecast Brazil 1997/98 orange juice production at 1.22 million tonnes.
The attache's 1997/98 export forecast of 1.16 million tonnes matched the department's estimate.
